title: Gandhi and His Eldest Son Harilal
text:
Harilal was the eldest of Mohandas Gandhi's four sons, born in 1888. He grew up partly in South Africa while his father led the Indian community's struggle there. Harilal joined the campaigns and went to jail several times, earning the nickname "Chhota Gandhi," little Gandhi.

But father and son clashed. Harilal wanted a formal education and to study law in England, as his father had. Gandhi, who had turned against Western schooling and personal ambition, refused, and twice gave an opportunity to study in England to others instead. Harilal also married young, against his father's wishes. In 1911 he broke away, leaving South Africa, and later broke openly with his father.

His life went from failure to failure. His business ventures collapsed, his wife died in the 1918 influenza epidemic, and he struggled with alcohol and debt. In 1936 he converted to Islam and took the name Abdullah, a step that pained his parents, though he later returned to Hinduism. His mother Kasturba pleaded with him in a public letter to give up drink.

Gandhi wrote to and about his son with a mixture of love, sternness and regret, and admitted that he might have failed him. Harilal outlived his father by only a few months. He died, ill and poor, in a Bombay hospital in June 1948.
lesson: A parent devoted to great causes must not forget the child at home. Principles applied to a son without listening to him can cost the relationship.
people: Mohandas Gandhi, Harilal Gandhi, Kasturba Gandhi
source: Chandulal Bhagubhai Dalal, Harilal Gandhi: A Life (2007); Gandhi's collected letters; Rajmohan Gandhi, Mohandas (2006)
